a: A drug that selectively relieves pain by acting in the CNS or on peripheral pain mechanisms, without significantly altering consciousness.
Opioid (morphine-like), nonopioid (NSAIDs) and adjuvant analgesics (anticonvulsants like gabapentin, pregabalin; antidepressants like amitriptyline, duloxetine).
Natural: morphine, codeine. Semisynthetic: heroin, pholcodine, ethylmorphine. Synthetic: pethidine, methadone, fentanyl, remifentanil, tramadol, tapentadol.
Analgesia, respiratory depression, sedation, euphoria, miosis, muscular rigidity, reduced GI motility, physical dependence (morphine type).

q: Which receptor causes dysphoria and psychotomimetic effects?
a: κ (kappa). Naloxone-resistant dysphoria is put down to σ receptors.

q: Endogenous ligands for μ, κ and δ?
a: μ: endomorphins 1 and 2 (β-endorphin binds strongly too). κ: dynorphin A. δ: leu- and met-enkephalins.
Gi/Go-coupled: ↓ adenylyl cyclase (cAMP), opens K⁺ channels (μ, δ) and closes N-type Ca²⁺ channels (κ) → hyperpolarisation and ↓ transmitter release.
Pro-opiomelanocortin (POMC), which also gives γ-MSH, ACTH and lipotropins.
